attacksRun.attack: The obligation set omits the recovery-ceremony cell that the live DR-112 row names
attacksRun.evidence: I raised this because the live DR-112 row enumerates four elements - reviewed state machine, air-gap/removable-media fixtures, recovery ceremony, audit/waiver expiry - and G08 v2's dr112Split names the same four cells, yet no obligation is titled for the ceremony. It is covered, split across two obligations rather than dropped. Live v8 carries a recoveryCeremony key whose shape array specifies the ceremony design and states 'Ceremony validity (key, threshold, expiry of the recovery envelope, and recoveryAuthorityShape) is this row; numbers are reserved', and recoveryAuthorityShape.standing reads 'SHAPE ONLY. No quorum, participant list, or officer is minted (OD-112-1 remains RESERVED).' So the shape is specified contract law, carried by OBL-CONTRACT-V8, and the unminted numbers are carried by OBL-RESERVED-NUMBERS as OD-112-1. The dispatch prohibition is calibrated the same way: it forbids inventing a ceremony implementation, not a ceremony design, because the design already exists.

observationsNotFindings: The reserved-numbers handling is the strongest part of this artifact and worth naming. Reproducing OD-112-1 through OD-112-4 as a whole object, dict-equal to G08 v2's, is the hardest form of quotation to fake and the easiest to check, and it keeps the four reservations legible without supplying a single value. The OD-112-4 entry is particularly careful: it records the waiver as expiry-bearing and explicitly 'not a number', which is exactly the distinction a later product act has to preserve.

OBL-ADVISORY-HONESTY is a category the sibling joins do not carry, and it is the right call. Traveling advisories are neither leftover-design nor discharged work, and giving them their own bucket with rideStanding honesty keeps them visible without letting them be mistaken for either. CODEX-V8-A1 in particular is bookkeeping about how the Codex v7 verdict is pinned, which would otherwise have no home on this row at all.

The recovery-ceremony cell is covered but only implicitly, split between OBL-CONTRACT-V8 for the shape and OBL-RESERVED-NUMBERS for the numbers, with no obligation named for it. That is substantively correct and I did not charge it, but the live DR-112 row and G08 v2's dr112Split both enumerate recovery-ceremony as a distinct cell, so a reader checking cell-by-cell will not find a matching obligation id and has to reconstruct the split as I did. A successor might make the mapping explicit.

Two of this row's obligations ride DR-110 and DR-113, neither of which is closed, and the G08 execution limb waits on fixtures that do not exist. DR-112's practical remainder is therefore wider than its two leftover-design entries suggest. The join does not claim otherwise.

It is not an application of v8, not a recording of G08 v2, not a seal, not a SATISFIED of DR-112, and not a QUALIFIED. Leftover-design remains open on OBL-G08-FX-AUTHORING and OBL-RESERVED-NUMBERS. decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. Both verbatim reproductions are exact: namedCorpusNotAuthored is element-wise equal to live G08 v2's four classes, and reservedNumbersVerbatim is dict-equal to G08 v2's reservedNumbersRemainReserved across all four OD-112 keys, values included - the hardest quotation in the file to fake and the easiest to check. All 9 recordedInputs and 6 structured pins recompute with zero mismatches, and the join records the distinct verdict strings ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES 0/0 for Claude and ACCEPT 0/0 for Codex rather than flattening them, matching both the live verdicts and D-105. Four of my own attacks looked like hits and dissolved on checking. The recovery-ceremony cell that the live DR-112 row names has no obligation of its own, but live v8 carries a recoveryCeremony shape and a recoveryAuthorityShape marked SHAPE ONLY with OD-112-1 reserved, so the design sits in OBL-CONTRACT-V8 and the numbers in OBL-RESERVED-NUMBERS - which is also why the dispatch forbids inventing a ceremony implementation rather than a ceremony. The citation 'G08 doesNotClaim' names no JSON key, but the quoted sentence is a first-class entry at G08 v2 .doesNot[6] and the token doesNotClaim appears in G08 v2's own prose immediately before that same sentence. A filtered read of D-105 appeared to say G08 is SATISFIED; the full block reads 'G06/G08 stay named-not-authored / not QUALIFIED', and that was my filtering. And OBL-G08-HARNESS-SPEC at leftoverDesign false while G08 v2 is accepted-but-unrecorded is the settled repo-wide convention, as verified across seven families. The advisories are handled well: both are carried in their own honesty bucket with the correct verdict-side identifiers, neither treated as leftover-design nor discharged, and I confirmed by reading them that they are genuinely distinct findings as D-105 states. No reserved value is supplied anywhere. Flagged without charging: the recovery-ceremony mapping is implicit rather than named, and two obligations ride DR-110 and DR-113, both still open. 21 attacks run, 21 refuted.
